notes:
## Page content and mathematical rereading

The page has two authorial circled 3s, one beside an abandoned upper calculation block and one before the live paragraph. The thin grey 6 at lower left is another hand's foliation. No title or date is written.

The discarded work gives compositions involving p0, p12, p13, rho and sigma, followed by repeated coordinate permutations/projections. Every repetition is retained, including the separate upper tuple with doubtful first x and middle x|z, the bare z,x,y and the doubled closing parenthesis in the rho²sigma₂ row. Three long diagonal strokes and a sweeping left/bottom boundary cancel this upper draft as a block; they are not ordinary diagram arrows.

The live paragraph says that when E0 is reduced to a point (written with the short form p and raised t), delta0 and delta1delta0 make E1 and E2 pointed sets, and the written groups G2,G3 respect the pointing. The page then adds the maps delta1 and p12 and lists five supplementary relations. A smaller compartment works with delta2; adjacent live and canceled equations and a repeated E1/E2 diagram remain individually transcribed within the integrated drawing. This describes the claims on the page; no proof verification or computation was performed by this reader.

Whole formulas were re-read wherever a label, index or state was at issue. The four group signs have enclosing G bowls and low inward returns, not S forms. Every delta/rho index and all four under-bracket labels were checked. In the underlined right-hand relation, the RHS really has two short upright numeral strokes after p, unlike the clear 2 on the left. The candidate therefore preserves p11 at medium confidence even though p12 recurs elsewhere; this is a literal possible slip, not a repaired equality. The lower diagram retains its written delta1 label.

## Revisions, placement and graphical marks

The separate canceled opening Donc./On a. remains uncertain. In the following canceled phrase the initial delta1 is exposed enough to recover, while the final les/le is still partly covered by the stroke. The et p12 above the later prose is live and attaches after delta1 by a curved leader; the curve does not supply a parenthesis. The quoted ponctués remains an independent marginal parenthetic by the first paragraph.

The top coordinate/projection diagram has a barred tail and two distinct right-facing chevrons on its first mapping; its two lower arrows have ordinary single heads. The later rho continuation instead has a little open loop at the right terminal. The last mapping has a square downturned right terminal with a lower leftward return. These endpoints are encoded literally as drawing geometry, without substituting a uniform mapsto. All tuple letters remain ordinary mathematical node text. Each complete discarded diagram is inside a deleted wrapper around an indivisible mbox, so its arrow paths as well as its nodes carry the cancellation state; the paragraph-producing diagram wrapper stays outside. The main live p12 arrow is straight and leftward; delta1 runs below on a rightward curve. The bottom repeated diagram has the same directions and a shallower lower curve.

The inner compartment occupies the lower right of the outer frame and shares its right and bottom borders. The outer frame has separate upper-left and lower-left joins and an overrun right upright; the compartment has a separately started left upright and a top rule ending in a small right arrowhead. Marginal typesetting follows the supplied conventions; source positions and the shared boundary are documented. The long line under the live p12sigma3=sigma p11 is an underline. The repeated equation and separate id-like mark below it have dense hatching. In the repeated equation, the initial p is exposed but its 12 subscript remains uncertain; sigma3 and final p12 are exposed, while the intervening equals/sigma also remains doubtful. The separate short entry remains doubtful as id.

## Edge, spelling and witnesses

The ending of respectent touches the right paper edge. The low e-like loop distinguishes it from H's respectant, but the final compressed n/t cannot be split with certainty, so respect followed by unsure ent is retained. No off-edge punctuation is supplied. The right E2 of the lower diagram also approaches the edge, but its E and index2 remain visible.

Both point abbreviations have raised t and are not expanded. The stop in ens. is visible. The main phrase is singular la ponctuation; the later phrase is plural les ponctuations. Paired quotation ticks, accents and actual punctuation are retained. H's connective summaries (Le calcul de, est mené en coordonnées, enfin and its long notes) are not source prose and are excluded from correction counts as editorial. TeX thin spaces are likewise not commas on the page.

There was no actual proof check, independent re-proof, computation, formal certificate or mathematical use-check by this reader. The record therefore has no check events.

### Root checks prompted by the last leaf

Symbolic substitution, saved in `records/151_007_computation.json`, checks the cancelled top projection equality, rho-sigma equality, the repeated p0 p12 sigma1 equality, and delta1 sigma(x,y)=(x,y,y). The cancelled intermediate composition rho^2 sigma2 should return (x,z,y) in this coordinate model, whereas the written continuation reads (y,x,z); the cancelled source trial is retained literally. These are checks of that example only. The point of preserving the cancellation is independent of whether an individual trial is correct.

The right-hand live underlined equality visibly ends **sigma p11**. Its two final index strokes are short uprights, unlike the separate hook-and-foot2 in the same line's p12. With p11 interpreted as repeated-coordinate projection, sigma p11(x,y,z)=(x,x), while p12 sigma3(x,y,z)=(y,x). The literal equality fails for distinct x,y; p12 in place of p11 would give the valid relation repeated elsewhere on the page. The clear11 is retained at medium confidence, not silently replaced. Events `151-007-coordinate-07` and `08` record that distinction. The live sigma2 delta2=delta2 identity checks correctly in the coordinate example.

For the pointed specialization, let e1=delta0(*) and e2=delta1(e1). The prior relations make e1 fixed by sigma and e2 fixed by rho and sigma1. Under the stated permutation-generator interpretation, they are the group-fixed marked points. Also p12(e2)=sigma(e1)=e1, while delta1(e1)=e2 by definition. The three values in the lower-right box follow from delta2=rho^2 delta1 and rho^3=id applied to the three values in the large box. The precise conditional argument is recorded as `151-007-pointed-consequences`; no general sufficiency or completeness theorem for the relations has been proved here.
